item.problem_title: Negative controls, proxies and validation data are not integrated into a standard emulation workflow
item.problem_statement: A correctly implemented emulation prevents specific design-induced temporal biases and does not create exchangeability. Active-comparator new-user designs, high-dimensional propensity scores and richer clinical measurement all reduce residual confounding without guaranteeing it. The tools that address what remains, negative control outcomes and exposures, instrumental variables, proximal causal learning and external validation samples, identify under distinct and partly untestable assumptions and sometimes target different estimands. They therefore cannot be mechanically ordered or combined: doing so requires an explicit joint model aligned to one estimand, and no such model is in use, so there is no convention for reporting what each tool contributed or for reconciling them when they disagree. item.problem_title: Code, phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not available for emulations
item.problem_statement: The TARGET statement asks for the target protocol, its data mapping, the estimands, the assumptions, the estimates and the sensitivity analyses, and is a transparency instrument rather than a risk-of-bias certification. An emulation is not externally auditable when its final analysis code, its complete versioned phenotype logic and its weight diagnostics are unavailable, and in current practice they are: most emulations are irreproducible in operative detail despite faithful protocol reporting. Where the real data cannot be shared, code plus a documented schema, a container and synthetic fixtures establishes that the pipeline executes and what it does; it does not reproduce the published estimate, and auditability rather than reproduction is what such a release can deliver. Material protocol amendments belong in a versioned decision log, which nothing currently requires.

item.problem_title: Emulation is proposed for non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions and assignment units are not defined
item.problem_statement: Interference, combination therapies, multiple treatment versions and non-pharmaceutical interventions all strain the two-arm, individually assigned, well-defined-intervention assumptions the standard emulation protocol makes. Policy interventions are the sharpest case: delivered to a place or an organization rather than a person, varying in content by implementer, arriving gradually rather than on a date, and often with no comparable version of not receiving them. A policy emulation therefore has to specify the assignment unit, the timing, the comparator, the intervention versions or a stochastic rule over them, the exposure mapping under interference, and a cluster-level estimand. item.paper: A trial emulation approach for policy evaluations with group-level longitudinal data.
item.evidence: A concrete protocol is supplied for a policy intervention: cohort-specific target trials, an explicit time zero for comparison units that never adopt, event-study placebo checks, and cohort-weighted aggregation over 17 cohorts. What it does not supply is a definition of the treatment. Stay-at-home orders differ by state, one tracker's definition is adopted, and heterogeneous requirements are deliberately packaged into a single exposure with the consistency assumption acknowledged as possibly violated.

verdicts.reason: Reporting numerical differences between observational and trial estimates on risk-ratio and risk-difference scales is more informative than a binary replication label. The quoted regulatory-agreement rule remains binary and does not provide a general comparison with joint uncertainty or diagnose estimand mismatch.

item.problem_title: Replication is reported as a binary label rather than as a calibrated comparison of estimands
item.problem_statement: Agreement between an emulation and a trial is informative only when the estimands, populations and measurements are close enough to be comparable, and better design alignment is empirically associated with stronger concordance. The benchmarking programs report this in graded form. What is cited downstream is a binary label, usually derived from interval overlap or direction agreement, and that label discards magnitude and uncertainty and cannot diagnose why two estimates differ: two studies estimating the same quantity imprecisely agree by that criterion, and two estimating different quantities precisely disagree. No reported measure, graded or binary, separates estimand mismatch from random error, because doing so requires aligning the estimands first and then reporting a paired contrast with joint uncertainty, which no benchmarking report currently does as a matter of course.
item.paper: Randomized Trial Replication Using Observational Data for Comparative Effectiveness of Secukinumab and Ustekinumab in Psoriasis: A Study From the British Association of Dermatologists Biologics and Immunomodulators Register.
item.evidence: Three agreement metrics are computed, and the standardized difference is a genuinely calibrated comparison: last observation carried forward with matching gave 0.009 for the risk ratio and minus 0.003 for the risk difference. What remains binary is the verdict that gets carried forward, because regulatory and estimate agreement are pass or fail labels that flip between matched and weighted analyses of the same 1231 patients, and no rule says which label the field should record.

item.evidence: Difference-in-differences estimates on the absolute scale are computed for every outcome, which is a calibrated comparison of estimands rather than a pass or fail label: -2.1% (CI -5.9 to 1.7) for lowest oxygen saturation and 2.5% (CI -8.1 to 13.6) for severe hypoxemia. What it does not close is the decision rule. The agreement criteria were not prespecified, no minimal clinically important difference was set, and the findings are consequently labelled exploratory.

item.problem_title: Inference conditions on a fixed target trial that was in fact selected after seeing the data
item.problem_statement: Eligibility thresholds, comparators, grace periods, washout windows and outcome definitions are routinely revised after investigators inspect the data. When outcome-relevant information from the analysis data is used to select among candidate protocols, a confidence interval calibrated for a protocol fixed in advance need not have nominal coverage for the selected estimand, unless the selection is incorporated into the inference or separated out through independent data. Saying so requires naming the target of inference and whether the coverage claimed is conditional on the selection or marginal over it, and applied reports do neither. item.problem_title: No decomposition separates scientific-target mismatch from protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error
item.problem_statement: Three trials are in play in any emulation and only one is usually named: the ideal trial that would answer the decision-maker's question, the target trial the investigator specifies, and the emulation the data support. Specifying the target trial closely around the available data conceals the distance between the first two, and the paper reports one estimate as though the chain were tight. What is missing is not an additive decomposition; that generally does not exist, because the transitions change populations, interventions, outcomes and scales, so the discrepancies do not add. What is missing is a documented lineage: the change from the decision question to the operational causal estimand, the assumptions mapping that estimand to an observed-data functional, and the estimation uncertainty, each recorded separately so a reader can see which step carries the load. item.paper: Improving rheumatoid arthritis comparative effectiveness research through causal inference principles: systematic review using a target trial emulation framework.
item.evidence: The audit is component-wise, which is the first half of a decomposition: failures are attributed to eligibility (61%), causal contrast (81% undefined), assignment (42%), follow-up (six studies with no defined end) and analysis, rather than pooled into a single risk-of-bias verdict. It stops short of the second half. No component is assigned a magnitude, the direction of bias is left as either direction, and mapping loss is not separated from estimation error in any of the 31 studies.

Including selected donor attributes in outcome and weight models does not establish that those attributes exhaust relevant versions or give a criterion for deciding when versions may be pooled.

item.problem_title: No procedure defines clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions
item.problem_statement: Estimating a per-protocol effect requires the sustained strategy and its relevant treatment versions to be clinically specified first; artificial censoring with inverse probability weighting is one valid estimation route rather than a requirement. Beneath the mechanics sits the question the mechanics assume answered: what counts as the same treatment. Real treatments differ by dose, route, provider, formulation, combination and adherence pattern, and two regimens sharing a label may not satisfy consistency. Clone-censor-weight handles a patient compatible with several predefined strategies and does not decide whether versions should be pooled into one. Observed data can expose heterogeneity across versions and cannot establish that versions are irrelevant, so the pooling decision is clinical. item.paper: Estimating conditional survival benefit for the allocation of scarce resources.
item.evidence: Multiple versions of treatment are named as a first-class identification problem rather than assumed away, and a procedure is supplied: donor age, rescue offer status, cause of death, donation after cardiac death and center proximity enter both the weight model and the marginal structural model, so a counterfactual is defined per organ rather than per transplant. What is not closed is the equivalence class itself. The five donor variables are asserted to exhaust the relevant variation in liver quality with no evidence for that sufficiency, and no criterion is given for when two organs count as the same treatment.
